sentences: Updated October 28, 2026: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon , the second Gemini 4 model.
It ranks first on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0 at 59, but only cyber defenders can use it for now.
Gemini 4 Argon, public since October 13, is still the newest Gemini 4 model you can use, and our Gemini 4 Argon guide covers it in full.
Google announced Gemini 4 Argon , the first Gemini 4 model, on September 30, 2026 , and after two weeks with vetted cyber defenders only, opened it to paying users on October 13, 2026 .

The road there began on July 21, 2026 , when Google wrote, in the announcement of a much smaller model, that “we have started our most ambitious pre-training run yet, for Gemini 4, and are excited by the progress”.
That was the first time Google confirmed the name in its own words.
Fello AI puts GPT-6, Claude 5.5, Gemini 4 Argon, Grok 4.7 and more in one native Mac and iPhone app.
Ask ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini the same question in one window and keep the best answer.
To understand where we are, look at the recent official release cadence from Google.
The internet is full of speculation.
Even now that Gemini 4 has been released, posts about the next Gemini 4 model or about Argon reaching the free plan are often predictions rather than facts.
Google typically releases new models by updating their technical documentation and publishing a blog post on The Keyword .

It is important to understand the difference between a “model update” and a “new generation.” Google frequently pushes updates to existing models without changing the major version number, and the recent jump from Gemini 3 Pro to Gemini 3.1 Pro to Gemini 3.5 Flash is a perfect example.
Google naming the model in a blog post, as it did on July 21, was a genuine signal, but a signal about the roadmap and not about availability.

When the generation did arrive on September 30, it came with a post on The Keyword and announcements from Google DeepMind’s own accounts, but not with a public model ID, because the first release went to a closed group.
The public release on October 13 is the one that brought the API model ID, the model card and a dated entry in the Gemini release notes.
If you want to know is Gemini 4 released for real, do not rely on trending hashtags.
To confirm Gemini 4 availability, rely on official sources.

Consumers should watch the dated Gemini release notes , developers should check the API model catalog and changelog for new model IDs, and enterprise users should monitor the official enterprise model lists and the Google AI plans page.
Note: Below is inference based on Google’s public direction in agents, creation, and computer use (e.g., Project Mariner (agent prototype) ) and the current Gemini roadmap signals, not a leak.
We wrote these grounded expectations about Gemini 4 features before Argon was announced, and we have kept them, with each one checked against what Google published on September 30.
The 3.5, 3.6, 3.7 and 3.8 Flash releases raised the bar with frontier intelligence at Flash speed, and Gemini Omni introduced native video generation.

The next step will likely focus on how the AI acts and reasons over longer tasks, moving from “chatbots” to true “agents.” Pichai pointed the same way on the July 22, 2026 earnings call, calling coding and agentic coding an area where Google has “acknowledged we need to improve” and saying the next frontier depends on “much larger base models” .
Users are hoping for a more powerful Gemini 4 context window .
Current Gemini API models, 3.8 and 3.7 and 3.6 and 3.5 and 3.1 and 2.5 alike, generally support 1,048,576 input tokens (≈1M) .
Worth knowing before you plan around that number, Gemini 3.6 Flash retrieves only 54.0% on GDM-MRCR v2 at the full 1M mark, so a huge window is not the same as reliable recall across it.
Earlier Gemini 1.5 Pro releases supported up to a 2M token context window historically, but today’s competitive focus has shifted to reasoning and tooling.

We expect major improvements in deeper “System 2” thinking where the model takes time to reason before answering, better reliability with fewer hallucinations for enterprise use, and richer Computer Use that builds on the Gemini 2.5 Computer Use: automate your browser tools and the agentic gains already in the 3.7 and 3.8 Flash releases.

The September 15 Live models are the first public look at that direction: Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking reasons and speaks at the same time, narrating its progress through multi-step background tasks instead of going quiet while it works.
How it landed: Google calls Argon “built to sustain deep reasoning across complex, long-horizon workflows”.

The window did not grow: Argon has 1,048,576 tokens, but that limit now covers input and output together, and with the API’s new long-decode feature a single response can run to about 1 million tokens, against 64,000 on earlier Gemini models.
We also expect Gemini 4 multimodal capabilities to push past today’s baseline.

Gemini Omni Flash already accepts image, audio, video, and text input and generates editable video, and Google has since added a cybersecurity-tuned Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber , so Gemini 4 will likely extend toward longer-form video, real-time streaming, and tighter integration with agents.

Two September releases already move that way: agentic video understanding , added on September 1, lets Gemini search and inspect only the parts of a video it needs instead of ingesting every frame, and Gemini 3.8 Live reads visual input in near real time while it is still talking.
Imagine showing the AI a video of a broken appliance and asking it how to fix it.
A future Gemini 4 agent could watch the video, identify the part, and browse the web to find the replacement without prompting.

How it landed: Google pitches Argon at coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity defense and creative writing rather than at media creation, but its own benchmarks show it reading long video well, with a state-of-the-art 91.7% on LVBench.
It is crucial to practice “rumor hygiene” when reading about a Gemini 4 leak .
Not all sources are created equal.
Note on Project Mariner: This is evidence of Google’s agent direction (computer use), not Gemini 4 confirmation.
The last big Gemini 4 rumor was about a model called Carbon .

On October 9, 2026, Business Insider reported , citing internal documents and screenshots, that Google staff are testing Carbon, a newer Gemini 4 version, in Jetski, Google’s internal coding platform.
One employee said it “feels like Opus 5.5” for coding, but added that they would need to test it more.
According to the same report, Google has tested Gemini 4 models internally named Argon, Barium and Carbon, and an internal model called “Barium-B” was chosen to become the public Argon.
On October 28, Google settled it: Carbon shipped as a separate model, Gemini 4 Carbon , and the employee's comparison held up.
Carbon scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0, one point ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 , though for now only cyber defenders can use it.

Google has announced Gemini 4 pricing for the API: Argon costs an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens , with cached input 95% off, until November 30, 2026 , and $4 and $20 after that.
API access needs the paid tier.
Which consumer plans get it is a separate question, and there the naming has already evolved.

Subscriptions are now described via Google AI plan tiers , and the current ladder runs Free at $0 , Google AI Plus at $4.99 , Google AI Pro at $19.99 , and Google AI Ultra from $99.99 with a $199.99 tier on top for 20x the Pro limits.

As of October 23, 2026, Google’s plans page reads “Access to our Flash-Lite model” for the free tier and “Access to our Flash model” for Plus, with no version numbers, and lists “Access to Gemini 4 Argon” on both Google AI Pro and Ultra , next to Google’s Pro and Flash models.
That makes Pro the cheapest way to use Argon in the Gemini app.

Paid-first rollouts were already the pattern on the Flash line: in the Gemini app, Gemini 3.7 Flash reached you only through Spark , which needs AI Pro or Ultra, and Google excluded the European Economic Area, the United Kingdom, Switzerland and Nigeria from that rollout.
You can also learn how to claim free Google AI Pro for students , which now includes Argon, and our Gemini pricing guide and wider AI pricing comparison cover the plans in detail.
Google has not said whether Argon will ever reach Google AI Plus or the free tier.

Its multi-tiered approach keeps a Flash-class model for casual users and saves the frontier model for paying ones, and the shift from the old “AI Premium” to today’s “Pro” and “Ultra” levels points to a more specialized future for Google’s subscription ecosystem.
If Argon is not on your plan, or you want something cheaper for everyday work, the rest of the lineup covers most jobs.
To understand what is already possible, see our Gemini 3.5 review of what Google launched at I/O 2026 and our explainer on Gemini 2.5 vs Gemini 3 .
Note: Use *-latest aliases carefully, as they have automatically switched to newer Gemini models with each release.
You don’t need Gemini 4 to start high-value automation.
